verdict.rationale: ROS 2 documents launching a simulation with Gazebo and ROS 2, and a long-time user reports that ROS gives you sim 'for free' if you follow its conventions. That points to sim/real interchangeability through the shared topic and interface layer, but the docs never explicitly state that the same robot code runs unchanged against simulation and real hardware. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of running identical code on sim and the real robot, details of the swap mechanism (e.g. sim time, hardware-abstraction or controller interfaces), and hands-on corroboration of a sim-to-real transfer without rewrite.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can run the same robot code against simulation and the real robot without a rewrite

citations.quote: Goal: Launch a Simulation with Gazebo and ROS 2
ROS gives you data bagging, visualization, teleop and sim 'for free' if you follow its conventions
